<STRUCT_0001>
It is customary to require all the morphism sets
<MATH_0001> to be disjoint.
In this way a morphism <MATH_0002> has a unique <TEXTITOPEN_0001>source<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> <MATH_0003>
and a unique <TEXTITOPEN_0002>target<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> <MATH_0004>. This is not strictly necessary,
although care has to be taken in formulating condition (2) above
if it is not the case. It is convenient and we will often assume
this is the case. In this case we say that <MATH_0005> and <MATH_0006> are
<TEXTITOPEN_0003>composable<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if the source of <MATH_0007> is equal to the
target of <MATH_0008>, in which case <MATH_0009> is defined.
An equivalent definition would be to define a category
as a quintuple <MATH_0010>
consisting of a set of objects, a set of morphisms (arrows),
source, target and composition subject to a long list of axioms.
We will occasionally use this point of view.

Big categories. In some texts a category is allowed to have a proper
class of objects. We will allow this as well in these notes but only
in the following list of cases (to be updated as we go along).
In particular, when we say: ``Let <MATH_0001> be a category''
then it is understood that <MATH_0002> is a set.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The category <MATH_0003> of sets.
<STRUCT_0003> The category <MATH_0004> of abelian groups.
<STRUCT_0004> The category <MATH_0005> of groups.
<STRUCT_0005> Given a group <MATH_0006> the category <MATH_0007> of
sets with a left <MATH_0008>-action.
<STRUCT_0006> Given a ring <MATH_0009> the category <MATH_0010> of <MATH_0011>-modules.
<STRUCT_0007> Given a field <MATH_0012> the category of vector spaces over <MATH_0013>.
<STRUCT_0008> The category of rings.
<STRUCT_0009> The category of divided power rings, see
Divided Power Algebra, Section <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0010> The category of schemes.
<STRUCT_0011> The category <MATH_0014> of topological spaces.
<STRUCT_0012> Given a topological space <MATH_0015> the category
<MATH_0016> of presheaves of sets over <MATH_0017>.
<STRUCT_0013> Given a topological space <MATH_0018> the category
<MATH_0019> of sheaves of sets over <MATH_0020>.
<STRUCT_0014> Given a topological space <MATH_0021> the category
<MATH_0022> of presheaves of abelian groups over <MATH_0023>.
<STRUCT_0015> Given a topological space <MATH_0024> the category
<MATH_0025> of sheaves of abelian groups over <MATH_0026>.
<STRUCT_0016> Given a small category <MATH_0027> the category of functors
from <MATH_0028> to <MATH_0029>.
<STRUCT_0017> Given a category <MATH_0030> the category of presheaves of sets
over <MATH_0031>.
<STRUCT_0018> Given a site <MATH_0032> the category of sheaves
of sets over <MATH_0033>.
<STRUCT_0019>
One of the reason to enumerate these here is to try and avoid
working with something like the ``collection'' of ``big'' categories
which would be like working with the collection of all classes
which I think definitively is a meta-mathematical object.
